correctness.rationale: The source’s combined model can be built from common infection-contact, app-status, manual-link, recovery, and spontaneous-diagnosis marks. Increasing either tracing parameter only adds traceable edges. The analytic earliest-discrepant-birth argument shows that every infection realized under the stronger tracing graph is also realized under the weaker graph. The source then supplies the exact bridge from survival to the sign of the component threshold: extinction for \(R_{\mathrm{DM}}\le1\) and positive-probability unbounded growth for \(R_{\mathrm{DM}}>1\). This yields the two stated threshold implications without assuming value monotonicity of \(R_{\mathrm{DM}}\). The proof explicitly uses the source convention that recovered infected contacts remain tracing conduits.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies monotonicity of the combined manual/digital level-one curve as an unresolved mathematical question, precisely because its component reproduction number can move non-monotonically with either intervention parameter. The coupling theorem resolves that structural gap without requiring an explicit closed form for the mean-offspring matrix. It guarantees that once a tracing pair is subcritical, any coordinatewise stronger pair remains subcritical, which is the policy-relevant order property suggested by the source’s numerical contour.
